question.text: Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x)=x\sin x-4x^2$ in the interval $[-2, 2].$ Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization starting from the point $x_0=2.$ Round your answer to three decimal places.
question.explanation:
The Newton-Raphson process for optimization is

\[ x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f'(x_n)}{f''(x_n)}, \]

where $f'(x_n)$ and $f''(x_n)$ are the first and second derivatives of $f(x)$ evaluated at $x_n,$ respectively.

In our case, we have

\begin{align*} f'(x) &= (x\sin x-4x^2)' = \sin x+x\cos x-8x, \\[5pt] f''(x) &= (\sin x+x\cos x-8x)' = 2\cos x-x\sin x-8. \end{align*}

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

\begin{align*} x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{\sin(x_n)+x_n\cos(x_n)-8x_n}{2\cos(x_n)-x_n\sin(x_n)-8}. \end{align*}

Starting with $x_0=2,$ we have

\begin{align*} x_1 &= x_0 - \dfrac{\sin(x_0)+x_0\cos(x_0)-8x_0}{2\cos(x_0)-x_0\sin(x_0)-8}\\[5pt] &= 2 - \dfrac{\sin(2)+2\cos(2)-8(2)}{2\cos(2)-2\sin(2)-8}\\[5pt] &= 0.505\,007\ldots \end{align*}

For the second iteration, we have

\begin{align*} x_2 &= x_1 - \dfrac{\sin(x_1)+x_1\cos(x_1)-8x_1}{2\cos(x_1)-x_1\sin(x_1)-8} \\[5pt] &= (0.505\,007\ldots) - \dfrac{\sin(0.505\,007\ldots)+(0.505\,007\ldots)\cos(0.505\,007\ldots)-8(0.505\,007\ldots)}{2\cos(0.505\,007\ldots)-(0.505\,007\ldots)\sin(0.505\,007\ldots)-8}\\[5pt] &\approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ 0.025}, \end{align*}

rounded to three decimal places.

question.text: Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x)=\cos(4x)-x^2$ in the interval $[0.5, 1].$ Calculate the first two iterations of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization starting at the point $x_0=1.$ Round your answers to three decimal places.
question.explanation:
The Newton-Raphson process for optimization is

\[ x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f'(x_n)}{f''(x_n)}, \]

where $f'(x_n)$ and $f''(x_n)$ are the first and second derivatives of $f(x)$ evaluated at $x_n,$ respectively.

In our case, we have

\begin{align*} f'(x) &= (\cos(4x)-x^2)' = -4 \sin(4x)-2x, \\[5pt] f''(x) &= (-4 \sin(4x)-2x)' = -16 \cos(4x)-2. \end{align*}

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

\begin{align*} x_{n+1} &= x_n - \dfrac{(-4 \sin(4x_n)-2x_n)}{(-16 \cos(4x_n)-2)} = x_n - \dfrac{2 \sin(4x_n)+x_n}{8 \cos(4x_n)+1}. \end{align*}

Starting with $x_0=1,$ we have

\begin{align*} x_1 &= x_0 - \dfrac{2 \sin(4x_0)+x_0}{8 \cos(4x_0)+1}\\[5pt] &= 1 - \dfrac{2 \sin(4 \cdot 1)+1}{8 \cos(4\cdot 1)+1} \\[5pt] &= 0.878\,555\ldots \end{align*}

For the second iteration, we have

\begin{align*} x_2 &= x_1 - \dfrac{2 \sin(4x_1)+x_1}{8 \cos(4x_1)+1}\\[5pt] &= (0.878\,555\ldots) - \dfrac{2 \sin(4 (0.878\,555\ldots))+0.878\,555\ldots}{8 \cos(4(0.878\,555\ldots))+1} \\[5pt] &= 0.901\,873\ldots \end{align*}

Therefore, $x_1 \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0.879}$ and $x_2 \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{0.902},$ rounded to three decimal places.

question.text: Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x)=e^x-x^3$ in the interval $[3,4].$ Calculate the first two iterations of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization starting at the point $x_0=3.6$ Round your answers to three decimal places.
question.explanation:
The Newton-Raphson process for optimization is

\[ x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f'(x_n)}{f''(x_n)}, \]

where $f'(x_n)$ and $f''(x_n)$ are the first and second derivatives of $f(x)$ evaluated at $x_n,$ respectively.

In our case, we have

\begin{align*} f'(x) &= (e^x-x^3)' = e^x-3x^2, \\[5pt] f''(x) &= ( e^x-3x^2)' = e^x-6x. \end{align*}

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

\begin{align*} x_{n+1} &= x_n - \dfrac{e^{x_n}-3x_n^2}{e^{x_n}-6x_n}. \end{align*}

Starting with $x_0=3.6,$ we have

\begin{align*} x_1 &= x_0 - \dfrac{e^{x_0}-3x_0^2}{e^{x_0}-6x_0}\\[5pt] &= 3.6 - \dfrac{e^{3.6}-3(3.6)^2}{e^{3.6}-6(3.6)} \\[5pt] &= 3.752\,135\ldots \end{align*}

For the second, we have

\begin{align*} x_2 &= x_1 \dfrac{e^{x_1}-3x_1^2}{e^{x_1}-6x_1}\\[5pt] &= (3.752\,135\ldots) - \dfrac{e^{3.752\,135\ldots}-3(3.752\,135\ldots)^2}{e^{3.752\,135\ldots}-6(3.752\,135\ldots)} \\[5pt] &= 3.733\,407\ldots \end{align*}

Therefore, $x_1 \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{3.752}$ and $x_2 \approx \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{3.733},$ rounded to three decimal places.

question.text: Given that the function $f(x)=x^6-12x$ has a critical point in the interval $[1, 2],$ use the Newton-Raphson process for optimization starting from $x_0=1.5$ to estimate the critical point. Round your final answer to two decimal places.
question.explanation:
The Newton-Raphson process for optimization is

\[ x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f'(x_n)}{f''(x_n)}, \]

where $f'(x_n)$ and $f''(x_n)$ are the first and second derivatives of $f(x)$ evaluated at $x_n,$ respectively.

In our case, we have

\begin{align*} f'(x) &= (x^6-12x)' = 6x^5-12, \\[5pt] f''(x) &= (6x^5-12)' = 30x^4. \end{align*}

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

\begin{align*} x_{n+1} &= x_n - \dfrac{6x_n^5-12}{ 30x_n^4} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{x_n(30x_n^4) - (6x_n^5-12)}{30x_n^4} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{24x_n^5+12}{30x_n^4}. \end{align*}

Starting with $x_0 = 1.5,$ we have

\begin{align*} x_1 &= \dfrac{24x_0^5+12}{30x_0^4} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{24(1.5)^5+12}{30(1.5)^4} \\[5pt] &= 1.279\,012\ldots \end{align*}

Similarly, we have

\begin{align*} x_2 &= \dfrac{24x_1^5+12}{30x_1^4} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{24(1.279\,012\ldots)^5+12}{30(1.279\,012\ldots)^4} \\[5pt] &= 1.172\,682\ldots, \\[10pt] x_3 &= \dfrac{24x_2^5+12}{30x_2^4} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{24(1.172\,682\ldots)^5+12}{30(1.172\,682 \ldots)^4} \\[5pt] &= 1.149\,659 \ldots.\\[10pt] x_4 &= \dfrac{24x_3^5+12}{30x_3^4} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{24(1.149\,659\ldots)^5+12}{30(1.149\,659 \ldots)^4} \\[5pt] &= 1.148\,699 \ldots. \end{align*}

Notice that the last two approximations $x_3 \approx 1.15$ and $x_4 \approx 1.15$ are the same when rounded to two decimal places.

Therefore, the critical point of the function is $x \approx 1.15,$ rounded to two decimal places.

question.text: Given that the function $f(x)=e^x-3x^2+5$ has a critical point in the interval $[2, 4],$ use the Newton-Raphson process for optimization starting from $x_0=3.5$ to estimate the critical point. Round your final answer to two decimal places.
question.explanation:
The Newton-Raphson process for optimization is

\[ x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f'(x_n)}{f''(x_n)}, \]

where $f'(x_n)$ and $f''(x_n)$ are the first and second derivatives of $f(x)$ evaluated at $x_n,$ respectively.

In our case, we have

\begin{align*} f'(x) &= (e^x-3x^2+5)' = e^x-6x, \\[5pt] f''(x) &= (e^x-6x)' = e^x-6. \end{align*}

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

\begin{align*} x_{n+1} &= x_n - \dfrac{e^{x_n}-6x_n}{e^{x_n}-6} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{x_n(e^{x_n}-6) - (e^{x_n}-6x_n)}{e^{x_n}-6} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{e^{x_n}(x_n-1)}{e^{x_n}-6}. \end{align*}

Starting with $x_0 = 3.5,$ we have

\begin{align*} x_1 &= \dfrac{e^{x_0}(x_0-1)}{e^{x_0}-6} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{e^{3.5}(3.5-1)}{e^{3.5}-6} \\[5pt] &= 3.053\,190\ldots \end{align*}

Similarly, we have

\begin{align*} x_2 &= \dfrac{e^{x_1}(x_1-1)}{e^{x_1}-6} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{e^{3.053\,190\ldots}(3.053\,190\ldots-1)}{e^{3.053\,190\ldots}-6} \\[5pt] &= 2.864\,577\ldots, \\[10pt] x_3 &= \dfrac{e^{x_2}(x_2-1)}{e^{x_2}-6} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{e^{2.864\,577\ldots}(2.864\,577\ldots-1)}{e^{2.864\,577 \ldots}-6} \\[5pt] &= 2.833\,890 \ldots.\\[10pt] x_4 &= \dfrac{e^{x_3}(x_3-1)}{e^{x_3}-6} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{e^{2.833\,890\ldots}(2.833\,890\ldots-1)}{e^{2.833\,890 \ldots}-6} \\[5pt] &= 2.833\,149 \ldots. \end{align*}

Notice that the last two approximations $x_3 \approx 2.83$ and $x_4 \approx 2.83$ are the same when rounded to two decimal places.

Therefore, the critical point of the function is $x \approx 2.83,$ rounded to two decimal places.
